study: Tolan et al. (2020), Good Behavior Game + MyTeachingPartner (GBG+MTP) RCT for early-career teachers, J. School Psychology
eval_evidence: Authors are at University of Virginia (MTP developers — Downer, Pianta's center) and Johns Hopkins (GBG-in-schools developers — Ialongo, Bradshaw); the trial of the combined GBG+MTP program was conducted by the program developers' teams, not an independent third party.
developer_evidence: The intervention team delivered the 'intensive training workshop' and the biweekly MTP coaching cycles; MTP coaching is the developers' web-mediated model staffed by project MTP coaches. Developer/research team delivered the PD.
cascade_evidence: MTP coaches worked directly with each intervention teacher (biweekly coaching cycles, initial in-person then web-mediated); no train-the-trainer or lead-teacher cascade -> developer_direct.
counterfactual_evidence: Control teachers served as 'controls (business as usual)'; no alternative PD/program assigned to control. Standard BAU contrast.
coaching_evidence: 'Each teacher in the intervention condition was provided biweekly MTP coaching cycles throughout the training year' — recurring (biweekly) video-based coaching cycles focused on the teacher's own classroom practice -> frequent_inclass.
student_dose_evidence: GBG is a group-contingency classroom behavior-management game the teacher plays with the whole class, and MTP changes teacher-student interaction quality; both work THROUGH changing the teacher's regular classroom practice. No tutoring, pull-out, extra instructional minutes, or student-facing software dose is added.
maturity_evidence: Sample = novice teachers (first three years of teaching) in their 'training year'; achievement measured spring of that single training/implementation year. Teachers new to the program at the measurement wave -> first_year.
